themes_detail.label: Encampment Crisis Spike
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 25 THIS WEEK—a 440% spike above the 8-week baseline of 4.6 per week (z-score 5.5)—signaling a sudden acceleration of visible homelessness or street encampments across the Upper East Side that demands immediate investigation into what triggered the concentration.
evidence: 25 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.6-complaint weekly average over prior 8 weeks (440% increase)
Z-score of 5.5 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Represents largest single-week spike in dataset across all complaint categories
reporting_angles: Where are encampments clustering? Map complaint data to specific blocks or parks to identify hot zones.
Interview NYPD, NYC Homeless Services, and affected residents on whether new policies, weather, or service closures drove the spike.
Profile individuals living in encampments to understand why Upper East Side specifically is seeing this surge.

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Neglect
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints exploded to 7 THIS WEEK—an 833% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.8 per week (z-score 7.54)—indicating a sudden failure or gap in city sanitation services that is visibly degrading neighborhood cleanliness.
evidence: 7 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8-complaint weekly average (833% increase)
Z-score of 7.54 is the second-highest statistical anomaly in dataset
Suggests service disruption rather than ambient neglect, given historically low complaint volume
reporting_angles: Contact Sanitation Department to determine if crews were pulled, routes changed, or staffing gaps emerged this week.
Photograph affected streets to document visible debris or dirt accumulation.
Interview residents about timeline: when did street conditions visibly degrade relative to complaints filed?

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints jumped to 7 LAST WEEK—a 367% spike above the 8-week baseline of 1.5 per week (z-score 3.89)—suggesting either a contamination outbreak, a specific restaurant incident, or a surveillance artifact tied to dining in the Upper East Side.
evidence: 7 food poisoning complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.5-complaint weekly average (367% increase)
Z-score of 3.89 indicates rare statistical anomaly
Timing suggests cluster rather than seasonal pattern
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with Health Department inspection data and closure notices filed in past week.
Identify which restaurants or food vendors appear most frequently in complaints and investigate preparation conditions.
Interview Health Department to determine if outbreak investigation is underway or if complaints are unrelated incidents.

themes_detail.label: Real-Time Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Real-time enforcement complaints spiked to 8 LAST WEEK—a 357% increase from the 8-week baseline of 1.8 per week (z-score 6.45)—potentially indicating a new enforcement operation, increased police activity, or community perception of over-policing in specific neighborhoods.
evidence: 8 real-time enforcement complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.8-complaint weekly average (357% increase)
Z-score of 6.45 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Complaint type suggests community reaction to increased police or city enforcement activity
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD precinct to determine if new enforcement initiative, detail, or operation was deployed last week.
Interview residents and community board members about whether they perceived increased enforcement presence.
Review 311 complaint text to determine which enforcement actions triggered complaints (parking, quality-of-life, etc.).

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints peaked 3 WEEKS AGO at 12—a 243% spike above the 8-week baseline of 3.5 per week (z-score 6.94)—indicating a sustained or emerging waste management problem, though the signal has not persisted to this week and warrants follow-up.
evidence: 12 illegal dumping complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 3.5-complaint weekly baseline (243% increase)
Z-score of 6.94 indicates rare statistical anomaly
Spike has since moderated, suggesting either resolved issue or shift to different problems
reporting_angles: Geolocate the 12 complaints from 3 weeks ago to identify whether dumping was concentrated on specific streets or near particular properties.
Check Sanitation Department records for follow-up action, enforcement, or cleanup efforts tied to those locations.
Determine if the spike has genuinely subsided or if residents stopped reporting—survey community board or local social media.
